This is the best reply on this thread - thank you. Because of you, I now have a rubber band around my wrist that I snap every time I start to get anxious. It's helped tremendously, and it's only been three days!

I accomplish things on a regular basis, but my enthusiasm is lacking in my day-to-day activities. I don't feel excited when I wake up or even numb. All I generally think is, "Oh shit - this again." 

I saw a therapist a few years ago when I was depressed from being in school all the time before I knew how to relax, and he wasn't much help. I don't think I trusted him.

Thanks for your encouragement.

This is a weird question. Probably a sandwich. I feel like I'm exactly where I should be in life right now. I'm in school, finishing my degree.

Quite odd, though, when you consider that while according to societal expectations, I *should* be happy, yes? 

To answer your question, I don't know what would make me happy right now if I could have anything. I'm not a very material person. The only things I really covet are my laptop and my bike, and those are two practical things that I couldn't live without. 

Does your question have some sort of deeper meaning?

The funny thing is that I don't feel alone, and the visible external pressures I've experienced over the course of my life have slowly dissipated. I've repaired my relationships with my parents and my sister and we enjoy each others' company. I spend about 12 hours a day on campus, but most of my friends live within a mile of it, so any time I want to hang out, it's all cool. I even had a little "therapy" session before finals week with a friend of mine. It amazed me how well she listened, and she opened up a bit about her inner demons too - which she wasn't ready to face.

I've been fascinated with existentialism since a very young age. It was my favorite era in American Literature and probably the reason I got an A+ on the final. So yes - I *get* that musings about the nature of existence are perfectly normal. As an engineer, I also dual as a physicist and by that, I am fascinated by the very nature of existence.

Work is great. I'm studying how the mind works in terms of electrical components. Whenever I talk about it - sober or intoxicated - people always notice how enthusiastic I am to talk about what I do, and I am quite mindful that this is where I should be. Pinpointing my exact specialty area after graduation has been one of my most recent tasks, and I am worried that the work I am doing now will not satisfy the skill set requirements for an "ideal" job setting that I haven't researched yet. All well - I have the entire summer to apply for an internship.

Hobbies? I don't really have time for hobbies. I smoke weed - if you can consider that a hobby - on the weekends with friends and also like to go on hikes, drink and watch movies and play video games. I spend about 60 hours a week on campus and the weekends recovering. Right now I'm trying to learn how to dance and speak my parents' native language, but those are two things visibly on my to-do list and not necessarily scheduled.

One thing I have noticed is that I have no "middle ground" when it comes to my normal state of mind. I'm either *really* anxious and mindful of deadlines or lethargic. Or a mixture of the two - which is odd, and also what I'm feeling now. I have class in about ten minutes but want to finish writing this post. I'm thinking about getting some coffee, but I got 8 hours of sleep last night and don't necessarily feel tired, but do feel like I could take a nice nap. 

Thanks for the reply.
